answer: To raise the cost of a sybil flood, each new identity must escrow a scarce pearl of collateral that unlocks only after a long stretch of attested, non-overlapping work. A public beacon then lists which identities have actually paid that cost, so cheap clones never enter the trust set. If a bonded identity is later slashed, a relic of that slash stays on-ledger and bars the same capital from being recycled into a fresh voting bloc.
